text: Martha "Matty" Louisa Cocke (October 9, 1855 – August 15, 1938) was an American educator recognized as the first woman to serve as president of Hollins College in Virginia. She was born in 1855 to Charles Lewis Cocke and Susanna Virginia Pleasants Cocke, one of nine children, and grew up on the grounds of the Hollins Institute, which her father founded and supervised as superintendent. She graduated from the collegiate department in 1874. Early in her career, she worked as a secretarial assistant to her father before becoming an instructor of English, French, German, and mathematics two years after graduation. In 1884, she was appointed registrar and librarian. Her father owned the deed to the school due to money owed by the trustees; after his death in 1901 and the predecease of his eldest brother, the heir apparent, the remaining heirs selected Matty Cocke as president. Although she avoided public events, she was well-liked on campus, and students established a short-lived literary society in her honor; beginning in 1930, they sang to her annually on her birthday. Under her leadership, the Institute experienced significant growth: faculty and staff expanded from about forty to more than sixty by 1933, over a dozen new buildings were constructed, and prominent intellectuals visited campus regularly. The school began awarding an A.B. degree in 1903 and officially changed its name to Hollins College in February 1911. By the time she retired in 1933, the institution had adopted a four-year college curriculum and achieved full accreditation. Upon retirement, she transferred ownership of the college from the family to a public board of overseers. In 1926, she received an honorary Doctor of Laws from Roanoke College. She died at home at Hollins College on August 15, 1938, and is buried in the family cemetery on campus. Her personal papers are held by Hollins University, and she is listed on the Wall of Honor of the Virginia Women's Monument.
